result_policy.help_setup_description: Understand how this checklist definition will turn failed answers into an overall result after it is published.

result_policy.open_help: Explain how the checklist result is calculated
result_policy.default_pass_body: The result remains Pass unless the simple override or a configured group matches failed answers.
result_policy.any_failure_active_body: This checklist fails as soon as any question is answered Fail. Configured groups are preserved but are not evaluated while this override is active.
result_policy.any_failure_inactive_body: The simple override is off. Configured groups decide whether failed answers change the overall result.
result_policy.root_groups_body: Top-level groups are evaluated independently. Any matched top-level group can change the checklist result.
result_policy.no_groups: No failure groups are configured, so this checklist will pass regardless of failed answers until a group is added or the any-failure override is enabled.
result_policy.group_logic_modes: A group can match when any item, all items, at least a number of items, or at least a percentage of items match. A nested group counts as one item in its parent.
result_policy.ancestor_gating_body: A nested group's result applies only when every parent above it also matches.
result_policy.severity_body: When several matched groups apply, the strongest result wins: Fail, then Pass with considerations, then Pass.
result_policy.comments_body: Comments provide supporting evidence but do not change the calculated result.
result_policy.runtime_shortcut_matched: The checklist failed because the any-failure override is active and at least one question failed.
result_policy.runtime_shortcut_passed: No question has failed, so the checklist currently passes under the any-failure override.
result_policy.runtime_no_group_matched: No configured result group matched, so the checklist currently passes.

checklist_schema.title: Checklist schemas
checklist_schema.definition_help: Define bilingual sections and Pass/Fail questions with language independent codes, then group failed answers into a result policy.
checklist_schema.rules_help: A checklist passes by default. Enable the simple any-failure override or configure nested groups that change the result when selected questions fail.

policy.help: Use the simple override when every failed question should fail the checklist. For more precise behavior, turn it off and combine failed questions into groups. Top-level groups act independently, and the strongest matching result wins.
policy.any_failure_fails_help: When enabled, one failed answer fails the whole checklist without requiring group configuration.
policy.shortcut_active_help: The groups below are preserved but ignored while this option is enabled.
policy.groups_help: Create top-level groups and nest subgroups to model combinations of failed questions. Any matched top-level group can change the result.
policy.no_groups: No failure groups have been configured. With the simple override off, the checklist will pass until a group is added.
policy.empty_group: Add a failed question or subgroup to define this group.
